### 1. Architecture Overview
GlobalConfig is defined in Prometheus `config/config.go` and is embedded/consumed by downstream projects (Thanos ruler, Mimir, Grafana Alerting) via the Prometheus config library (`github.com/prometheus/prometheus/config`). The ScrapeInterval field is currently a `model.Duration`. Changing it to a new typed Duration with validation will break any code that constructs GlobalConfig or assigns `model.Duration` to `ScrapeInterval` or that relies on zero/default handling. The change cascades to:
- Prometheus core parsing/validation (Load/UnmarshalYAML, defaults, tests).
- Thanos Ruler (builds Prometheus config.Config and GlobalConfig for remote write).
- Mimir ruler/notifier and alertmanager integrations (builds Prometheus config.Config).
- Grafana NG Alert sender (builds Prometheus config.Config).

### 2. Detailed Analysis

#### Prometheus (repo: prometheus)
- `config/config.go` defines `type GlobalConfig struct { ScrapeInterval model.Duration ... }` and UnmarshalYAML defaulting/validation (ensures timeout <= interval, defaults on zero) at lines ~464–687. Changing the type requires updating the struct, default constants, and comparison logic in UnmarshalYAML and isZero.
  - Evidence: `ScrapeInterval model.Duration` and UnmarshalYAML defaulting/validation at `config/config.go` lines 464–687. Defaults at lines 156–186 set `DefaultGlobalConfig.ScrapeInterval = model.Duration(1 * time.Minute)` and `ScrapeTimeout`, `EvaluationInterval`, etc.
- Tests: `config/config_test.go` exercises global config defaults, zero checks, and scrape interval > timeout (`TestScrapeIntervalLarger`, `TestGlobalConfig`, `TestGetScrapeConfigs`, `TestGetScrapeConfigs_Loaded`) and will need adjustment to new type and validation semantics.
  - Evidence: `config/config_test.go` section map shows `TestScrapeIntervalLarger`, `TestGlobalConfig`, `TestGetScrapeConfigs`, etc.
- Other Prometheus code importing config.GlobalConfig will need to accept the new type when constructing configs (e.g., main, remote write). No direct file retrieved beyond config.go, but downstream packages depend on GlobalConfig defaults.

#### Thanos (repo: thanos)
- `cmd/thanos/rule.go` imports `github.com/prometheus/prometheus/config` and constructs `config.Config{GlobalConfig: config.GlobalConfig{ExternalLabels: ...}}` for remote write setup (lines ~430–506). Any code assigning `model.Duration` into GlobalConfig or expecting `model.Duration` in struct literal will break.
  - Evidence: `cmd/thanos/rule.go` lines 430–506 build `config.Config{ GlobalConfig: config.GlobalConfig{ ExternalLabels: ... } }`.
- Flag wiring uses `extkingpin.ModelDuration` for rule eval interval, but that does not directly set GlobalConfig; still, if they later set ScrapeInterval, type mismatch will surface.

#### Mimir (repo: mimir)
- `pkg/ruler/notifier.go` and `pkg/ruler/notifier` constructs Prometheus `config.Config` in `buildNotifierConfig` using `config.AlertingConfig`; indirect impact if they ever set GlobalConfig/ScrapeInterval. Currently they return empty GlobalConfig defaults, so type change mostly affects compilation if they set durations elsewhere.
  - Evidence: `buildNotifierConfig` returns `&config.Config{AlertingConfig: config.AlertingConfig{...}}` (lines 104–139).
- Broader imports of `github.com/prometheus/prometheus/config` across Mimir (handlers, ingester, querier, distributor) will need to adopt the new Duration type when touching GlobalConfig/ScrapeConfigs.

#### Grafana (repo: grafana)
- NGAlert sender builds Prometheus `config.Config` in `pkg/services/ngalert/sender/sender.go` (`buildNotifierConfig`, `externalAMcfgToAlertmanagerConfig`), mostly AlertmanagerConfig; they import `github.com/prometheus/prometheus/config`. If any use of GlobalConfig/ScrapeInterval exists, type must be adjusted. Even without direct ScrapeInterval use, compilation will break if ScrapeInterval is referenced with `model.Duration`.
  - Evidence: `buildNotifierConfig` creates `&config.Config{AlertingConfig: config.AlertingConfig{...}}` at lines 265–289; AlertmanagerConfig.Timeout uses `model.Duration`.

#### Loki Promtail (repo: loki)
- `clients/pkg/promtail/config/config.go` defines GlobalConfig for promtail; not confirmed to embed Prometheus GlobalConfig. No direct ScrapeInterval tie seen in retrieved data; likely unaffected unless reusing Prometheus GlobalConfig.

### 3. Relevant Files

| Repo | File Path | Why |
|------|-----------|-----|
| prometheus | config/config.go | Defines `GlobalConfig` with `ScrapeInterval model.Duration`, defaults, UnmarshalYAML validation; must change to new typed Duration and adjust validation/defaults. |
| prometheus | config/config_test.go | Tests GlobalConfig defaults, zero checks, and scrape interval > timeout; must be updated for new Duration type/validation. |
| thanos | cmd/thanos/rule.go | Imports `github.com/prometheus/prometheus/config` and builds `config.Config` with `GlobalConfig`; will fail assigning old duration type; must adapt to new Duration. |
| mimir | pkg/ruler/notifier.go | Builds Prometheus `config.Config` for Alertmanager; imports `prometheus/prometheus/config`; must compile with new Duration type. |
| mimir | pkg/ruler/notifier.go (functions `buildNotifierConfig`, `amConfigWithSD`) | Uses `model.Duration` for timeouts; ensure compatibility if Duration type changes/propagates. |
| grafana | pkg/services/ngalert/sender/sender.go | Builds `config.Config` and `AlertmanagerConfig` using Prometheus config types; imports `prometheus/prometheus/config`; must adapt to new Duration type. |

### Impact Summary & Actions
- Breaking change: Any assignment or struct literal using `model.Duration` for `ScrapeInterval` must switch to the new typed Duration. Update constructors, defaults, and YAML parsing in Prometheus `config/config.go`, and adjust tests in `config/config_test.go`.
- Downstream consumers (Thanos, Mimir, Grafana) that import `prometheus/prometheus/config` must update their build of `config.Config`/`GlobalConfig` to use the new Duration type and handle validation failures if values are out of bounds.
- Search/build across all repos for references to `ScrapeInterval` or `GlobalConfig{` to ensure no remaining `model.Duration` assignments remain.

llm_condensed_answer:
SUMMARY: Changing the ScrapeInterval field in GlobalConfig from model.Duration to a new typed Duration will break any code that assigns model.Duration values to it, requiring updates in Prometheus core and downstream consumers. The change affects Prometheus's config parsing and validation, and cascades to Thanos, Mimir, and Grafana, which construct Prometheus config.Config objects that embed GlobalConfig.

FILES:
- prometheus/config/config.go — Defines GlobalConfig with ScrapeInterval model.Duration and validation logic that must be updated.
- prometheus/config/config_test.go — Contains tests for GlobalConfig defaults and interval validation that need adjustment for the new Duration type.
- thanos/cmd/thanos/rule.go — Builds config.Config with GlobalConfig and will break assigning old duration type.
- mimir/pkg/ruler/notifier.go — Constructs Prometheus config.Config for Alertmanager and must adapt to new Duration type.
- grafana/pkg/services/ngalert/sender/sender.go — Builds config.Config and AlertmanagerConfig using Prometheus config types, requiring updates for new Duration.
